proposals.evidence: The full DEDR 1 article gives Malayalam a, ā that, yonder; avan, avaḷ, avar, atu, ava that man, that woman, those persons, that thing, those things; atatu each, several; aṅṅu, aṅṅunnu there, thither; aṅṅane, aṅṅine that way, thus; aṅṅiṭam, aṅṅōṭu there; aṅṅiṭ-iṅṅiṭam here and there; atā…. The Malayalam survey form ayāḷ “third-person singular, male, honorific, remote” is proposed within this article family. Lindgren assigns the corresponding Tamil reflex to the same source cognate set.

The Malayalam survey form ivan “third-person singular, male, proximate” is proposed within this article family. Lindgren assigns the corresponding Tamil reflex to the same source cognate set.
